methodological_rigor.justification: The study employs a multi-layered mechanistic approach: (1) clinical validation in 63 patient-derived malignant pleural effusion (MPE) samples with Mann-Whitney U tests and appropriate group stratification; (2) in vitro functional assays using gain- and loss-of-function (overexpression transfectants, siRNA knockdown, stable shRNA clones) in authenticated EGFR-mutant NSCLC cell lines (HCC827, H1975) and resistant derivatives; (3) in vivo xenograft SCID mouse models (n=6/group) with Kaplan-Meier survival analysis; (4) TCGA-LUAD bioinformatics with GSVA and Spearman correlations with FDR correction; (5) ChIP assay providing direct mechanistic evidence of STAT3 binding to the ZEB1 promoter. Cell lines are STR-authenticated and mycoplasma-tested. Methods are well-documented with reagent sources, catalog numbers, and protocols. Limitations include reliance on a STAT3 inhibitor (S3I-201) and CCR2 antagonist (INCB3344) without genetic rescue of STAT3 in knockdown conditions (acknowledged by authors), and the mouse xenograft groups have modest n=5-6 per group. Statistical approaches are appropriate throughout.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: As a preclinical mechanistic study (LoE 5), the study has clear translational relevance: osimertinib resistance is a critical unmet clinical need affecting EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients who represent 40-50% of Asian and 10-20% of Western NSCLC patients. The CCL2-CCR2-STAT3/ERK-ZEB1 axis provides a novel actionable therapeutic target. Patient-derived MPE samples (n=63) anchor the clinical relevance of CCL2 upregulation in resistance. The proposed combination of STAT3 inhibition with osimertinib has direct translational potential, though no clinical correlation with outcomes was performed in the patient cohort.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript is well-reported with detailed methods including reagent sources and catalog numbers, IACUC approval numbers, IRB approval for patient samples, and RRID identifiers for cell lines. Statistical methods are clearly described with appropriate tests for each data type. Figure legends are comprehensive and specify biological replicates and error bars. Supplementary tables and figures are referenced throughout. Limitations are acknowledged in the discussion. No formal mechanistic reporting checklist is cited; raw data and code are not publicly deposited. TCGA data are publicly available.

novelty_literature.justification: The study defines a novel CCL2-CCR2-STAT3/ERK-ZEB1 signaling axis in osimertinib resistance, distinct from previously reported CCL2-AKT resistance mechanisms. The direct demonstration of STAT3 binding to the ZEB1 promoter via ChIP assay in resistant cells provides mechanistic specificity not previously shown in this context. Validation in patient-derived MPE samples from osimertinib-resistant patients is a meaningful clinical anchor. The finding that CCL2-mediated resistance operates through STAT3/ERK rather than AKT—contradicting prior reports—and the novel combination strategy (STAT3 inhibitor + osimertinib) reversing xenograft resistance are substantive novel contributions. The prior literature on CCL2 in EGFR-TKI resistance focused primarily on the AKT pathway.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-structured with a logical narrative from clinical observation (elevated CCL2 in MPEs) through mechanistic dissection to therapeutic validation. The introduction, results, and discussion are clearly written and appropriately contextualize findings within the NSCLC resistance literature. The proposed mechanistic model (Figure 8) effectively summarizes the signaling pathway. Limitations are forthrightly acknowledged. Some minor redundancy exists between results and figure legends. Overall writing quality is high for a mechanistic cancer biology manuscript.

key_strengths: Novel CCL2-CCR2-STAT3/ERK-ZEB1 axis mechanism of osimertinib resistance validated across multiple complementary experimental platforms (in vitro, in vivo, patient-derived MPE samples)
Direct ChIP evidence of STAT3 binding to the ZEB1 promoter in osimertinib-resistant cells provides mechanistic specificity
Clinical anchor: CCL2 upregulation confirmed in 63 patient-derived MPE samples from osimertinib-resistant NSCLC patients (p=0.0142)

Multi-layered functional validation: gain/loss-of-function with CCL2, ZEB1, and CCR2 using overexpression, transient siRNA, and stable shRNA; pharmacological validation with S3I-201 and INCB3344; carlumab neutralizing antibody
In vivo reversal of resistance by STAT3 inhibitor + osimertinib combination in xenografts
key_concerns: Genetic rescue experiments (constitutively active STAT3 in CCL2-knockdown resistant cells) were not performed, acknowledged as a limitation
Xenograft groups are modest (n=5-6 per group), limiting power for survival comparisons
S3I-201 and INCB3344 potential off-target effects not fully excluded by pharmacological approach alone
The relative contributions of STAT3 versus ERK1/2 downstream of CCL2 to ZEB1 upregulation are partially conflated—the mechanistic hierarchy between the two pathways is not fully resolved
Clinical patient cohort lacks formal statistical power calculation and individual patient outcome data (e.g., time-to-resistance)
chief_reviewer.rationale: A well-executed mechanistic study uncovering a novel CCL2-STAT3/ERK-ZEB1 resistance axis in osimertinib-resistant NSCLC with clinical validation in patient-derived samples and in vivo proof-of-concept. The multi-platform experimental design and ChIP mechanistic evidence distinguish this work from descriptive resistance studies. Suitable for a Tier 2 oncology or cancer biology journal (JIF 10-19) with minor revisions primarily to strengthen the mechanistic distinction between STAT3 and ERK contributions and add genetic rescue data if feasible.
